checkpoint_followup.source_policy: docs/product/FOUNDATION_006_CHECKPOINT_POLICY.md still specifies exactly four tasks, 90 minutes, pass three of four, three learner-result submissions per task, and unrestricted task navigation. This source was read on 26 October. No repo policy or implementation was changed.
checkpoint_followup.policy_mismatch: LATEST PRODUCT DIRECTION: each exam gets its own configured passing count later. The existing fixed-four/pass-three source is historical for that future configuration, but has not been edited. Before actual exam publication freeze its question count and required passed count. Do not extrapolate three-of-four, invent a percentage, or change quota/duration/retakes. No numeric decision is needed to continue design.
checkpoint_followup.sample_values: Ten question rows, Question 03, 30:00 remaining, Go comments and demonstration statuses are layout-only samples. The statement/signature/example placeholders deliberately define no exercise or curriculum. No real learner results or ten-question scoring are shown.
approved_design_direction: Internal source editor inside Checkpoint only.
Free question selection without passing previous questions.
Configure the passing count separately for each exam later; there is no fixed global four/pass-three rule for the future design.
Per-question drafts survive question navigation. Autosave to server with truthful Saving/Saved/Save failed states.
Temporary same-device offline drafts resync only while time and access allow. Saving is not Submit; later edits remain drafts until explicit resubmission.
Keep global Journey eligibility, authorization, accepted Judge verdicts, quota and deadline rules server-owned.
APPROVED: Run visible examples only, ungraded, no graded-attempt consumption. Submit is official evaluation; hidden tests remain private.
APPROVED: Run visible examples only, ungraded, no graded-attempt consumption. Submit is official evaluation; hidden tests remain private.
proposed_visual_spec: Desktop: persistent question rail, authored-statement pane and internal editor pane. Selected question and its draft/result remain separate.
Mobile: near-top timer/review controls, wrapping dynamic question choices, Statement/Editor/History tabs and legible editor. Preserve per-question state when changing tabs/questions.
Question count is data-driven; do not implement ten hardcoded records or a prerequisite chain between questions.

At 320/390/768/1440 widths allow editor-local horizontal code scrolling, readable statement text and adequate touch targets; no page overflow. Long question lists scroll within their region without hiding the selected item.
Timer and primary controls remain reachable with virtual keyboard/safe areas; exact sticky behavior requires actual device/browser validation.
History shows exact accepted source and safe verdicts, independently of a newer draft.
Review lists each supplied question with its draft state and accepted status; finishing still requires explicit irreversible confirmation.
existing_rules_preserved: Trusted server time governs deadline and accepted-before-deadline work. Browser time and reconnection do not extend the clock.
Finish closes new intake immediately after confirmation; unanswered items earn no credit and already accepted work continues evaluating.
System error remains an infrastructure outcome, not learner failure or a consumed learner-result submission.
Pending accepted results are not prematurely classified as failure. Mastery/unlock follow the applied server outcome.
Current authorization is required. Access removal must not reveal protected statement, source or history.

engineering_contract_gaps.drafts: Draft preservation/autosave/same-device offline recovery behavior is approved, but no save API or implementation is proven by images. Version model, local retention duration, cross-device conflicts and expiry/access cleanup require a conservative engineering specification.
engineering_contract_gaps.source_snapshot: Existing raw-file intake does not prove a browser-editor submit path. A new adapter must preserve exact evaluated bytes, required-file identity, task/attempt binding and immutable accepted receipt without altering Judge semantics.
engineering_contract_gaps.deadline_and_trust: An editor buffer is not a submission. Server authorization, attempt state, trusted deadline, quota and idempotency must be revalidated atomically at acceptance. No client-reported saved time or result is trusted.
engineering_contract_gaps.graded_vs_ungraded: Run semantics are approved: visible examples only, ungraded, no graded-attempt consumption; Submit official evaluation. Separate resource/rate settings, deadline/access gating, cancellation and immutable run-source/stale-output handling need engineering specification. There is no implemented Run endpoint in the inspected source.

proposed_safe_defaults_awaiting_decision: Key drafts by authenticated learner, immutable checkpoint attempt and question identity. Never reuse a draft across attempts or learners.

APPROVED behavior: per-question server autosave and truthful Saving/Saved/Save failed states. Proposed implementation: versioned saves with acknowledgement; a save is never grading or a submission receipt.

APPROVED behavior: temporary same-device offline draft and resync only while exam time/access permit. Conservative engineering proposal: scope by learner/attempt/question, validate current authorization/deadline on reconnect and require an explicit choice on cross-device conflicts; never overwrite a newer draft silently.

Define a bounded retention duration and expiry/access cleanup before implementation. Do not assume indefinite browser persistence or sync after time/access expires. No queued graded Submit or deadline auto-submission is authorized.
On session expiry block grading and require sign-in. On access removal hide protected work immediately; local recovery retention/purge is a security decision, not assumed by the screen.

At explicit graded Submit, capture the exact buffer bytes and original intent until acceptance is known. Uncertain acknowledgement reconciles the same intent; later deliberate revision uses a new intent under the existing allowance.
Only the accepted immutable snapshot is evaluated. Further editing never changes accepted bytes, stored verdicts or history.
At deadline or confirmed early finish, close new submissions; do not grade an unsent buffer automatically. Previously accepted work finishes under existing policy.
APPROVED: Run visible examples only, ungraded, no graded-attempt consumption; Submit official evaluation. Keep output and source association separate from official submission history.

Visible examples are approved. Specify separate Run rate/resource limits, deadline/access gating, resource isolation, cancellation, stale-response handling and source-snapshot identity before implementation. No hidden-test details or browser execution are implied.
No AI/code completion, anti-paste, browser lockdown, tab monitoring or proctoring is introduced. The internal editor does not establish cheating prevention.
acceptance_before_implementation: Review actual desktop/mobile composition; these are static images, not functioning editors.
Configure an explicit question count/pass count per exam before publication; numeric decisions are deferred, not a design blocker.
Specify retention/conflict/session/access details for the approved autosave behavior and specify remaining Run resource/lifecycle details before implementation.
Confirm direct selection across every authorized question and restoration of its draft, cursor/scroll and accepted status after switching.
Test server save acknowledgements, save failure, reload, reconnect, session expiry, access removal, offline edits and cross-device conflict; no silent overwrite or cross-user/attempt leakage.
Verify official immutable source snapshots, duplicate/uncertain requests, deliberate revision, quota and concurrent submit/deadline races.
Verify Run pending/result/error/stale-source display separately from official history; no inferred score, pass/mastery or graded-attempt effect.
Specify and test Run cancellation/resource/rate/deadline rules; never leak hidden-test data.
Verify finish confirmation, unsent buffer treatment, accepted late result, evaluating and infrastructure-blocked finalization.
Verify keyboard editor escape/focus behavior, labeled region/tab navigation, screen-reader status, virtual keyboard, zoom, long code and reduced motion.
Do not mistake static artifact QA for source tests or real authenticated execution.

run_design.interpretation: APPROVED visible-example-only, ungraded execution; no graded-attempt consumption. Submit official evaluation.
ui: Run and Submit are separate actions; Run output is outside official submission history.
Represent idle, pending, bounded output, execution error and infrastructure failure distinctly.
Proposed: show the source/version associated with a run and mark output stale after edits; never apply old output to a newer buffer.
Run again is conditional on the eventual approved rules; pending feedback never invents percentages or a completion time.
unresolved: separate numeric resource and rate limits
immutable run source identity and stale output

checkpoint_followup.publication_gate: Before publishing each real exam, configure and freeze its questions and passing count, validate the count against that definition and implement trusted aggregation. No missing threshold defaults or global pass-three fallback.
draft_engineering_recommendations: Use optimistic version checks on learner/attempt/question-scoped server drafts. Reject stale writes; retain both versions for an explicit recovery choice rather than silently overwriting newer work.

Temporarily scope offline recovery to the same authenticated learner, exam attempt and question. Do not put credentials in browser storage. Proposed conservative expiry: stop recovery sync at the trusted attempt deadline or access removal, and clear protected local recovery on logout/access removal. Exact retention/purge timing must be documented and tested; this recommendation is not a newly awarded exam entitlement.
Session expiry blocks grading and sync until the same identity is reauthorized within the exam window. Never auto-submit saved/offline code at deadline.
Keep draft persistence, official Submit snapshot and visible-example Run snapshot separate. Associate output with the exact source version; mark it stale after edits.
